text:
maria: Quick PSA — hit a weird cancellation edge in the Go generator sample app. When ctx is canceled mid-stream a background send goroutine sometimes keeps running and we eventually get a panic from writing to a closed socket.
kevin: ugh, can you paste the minimal snippet?
maria: sure — simplified:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
req := inference.GenerateRequest{Prompt: "..."}
gen := client.NewGenerator()
stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
go func() {
  for tok := range stream.Tokens() {
    // process token
  }
}()
// do other work; when ctx.Done() happens stream sometimes doesn't close the Tokens() channel
```
maria: Observed behavior: ctx.Done() -> parent returns, but Tokens() chan never closed in some runs; leak until goroutine panics on write.
paul: is this in the sample app or the runtime wrapper? could be our transport not noticing the context cancellation during a blocked write.
sophia: interesting — auth/token refresh interplay could cause blocked writes. if the auth middleware pauses while refreshing token the context might be canceled but the lower-level TLS write is still blocked.
kevin: another hypothesis: Stream(ctx) returns a stream object but its Close() is not auto-invoked on ctx cancel. We should document whether Stream honors ctx cancellation or require caller to call stream.Close(ctx).
ryan: fwiw, our Go SDK has two patterns elsewhere: 1) blocking Read that returns error on ctx cancel, 2) channels that close on cancel. We should pick one for generator consistency.
paul: also saw flaky auth retry behavior: if ctx canceled while token refresh is inflight, retry loop sometimes swallows the ctx error and sends a retry later, causing duplicate work client-side.
kevin: proposal: Stream(ctx) must guarantee that either Tokens() closes or Err() becomes context.Canceled promptly. Add a CloseWithErr(err) on stream to surface cancel reason.
maria: I sketched an API change in sample app:
```go
// Stream returns a stream where Tokens() is closed on ctx cancel and Err() returns final error
stream, err := gen.Stream(ctx, req)
// ensure caller can call stream.Close() in defer if they want deterministic cleanup
defer stream.Close()
for tok := range stream.Tokens() { ... }
if err := stream.Err(); errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) { // expected }
```
paul: sounds good. also consider: add deterministic Abort() on the generator to abort in-flight tokenization on server side (avoid wasted GPU cycles).
sophia: can we also add a short integration test that simulates slow network + immediate ctx cancel to catch regressions?
ci-bot: test/linux-amd64: TestGeneratorCancelLeak flaky (2/5) — see https://ci.internal/reports/17688/TestGeneratorCancelLeak
maria: I'll open an issue with the failing test log and a minimal repro. tagging @kevin @paul for API review.
kevin: quick UX note: the current Go sample apps show use of context.Background() in examples — that encourages ignoring cancellation. We should update docs to show proper ctx propagation and defer stream.Close().
sophia: agree. I can update the docs once the API shape is decided.
paul: FYI, auth team: if we change retry propagation we need to ensure the HTTP transport returns context.Canceled upstream immediately during token refresh failure.
ryan: for the runtime side, we can add a small timeout on socket writes so the goroutine can't block forever; that reduces leak windows while we fix higher-level flow.
maria: action items:
- maria: open issue + attach repro + CI links (I'll do now)
- kevin & paul: review API proposal (Close()/CloseWithErr/Abort)
- sophia: doc samples update after API lock
- ryan: add transport timeouts as mitigation
ci-bot: issue created: https://issues.internal/RED-2345 (contains logs and minimal repro)
maria: thanks y'all, will post PR once I have a passing minimal integration test. :thumbsup:
